column1: Which regex library underlies SQL Server 2025's regular expression functions?
column2:
RE2.
Do not assume that every JavaScript or Python regex feature is supported.
Review source

column1: What database compatibility level does SQL Server 2025 REGEXP_LIKE require?
column2:
170 or higher.
The SQL Server version alone does not satisfy this database-level requirement.
Review source

column1: How is REGEXP_LIKE used in a SQL Server WHERE clause?
column2:
As a predicate: WHERE REGEXP_LIKE(ColumnName, 'pattern').
Do not compare this Boolean predicate to the integer 1.
Review source

column1: Why use ^ and $ around a grouped validation pattern with default regex flags?
column2:
To require a match across the entire input string.
No unmatched prefix or suffix is allowed.
Review source

column1: In SQL Server regex, what does . match when the s flag is absent?
column2:
One character other than a newline.
The s flag allows the dot to match a newline too.
Review source

column1: Which characters does SQL Server regex \w match?
column2:
ASCII letters, digits, and underscore: [0-9A-Za-z_].
It is not a class for every Unicode letter.
Review source

column1: What controls regex case sensitivity instead of SQL Server's linguistic collation?
column2:
The regex flags, such as c or i.
Regex matching does not honor SQL linguistic collation rules.
Review source

column1: Why does (?=...) fail in a SQL Server 2025 regex matching pattern?
column2:
The RE2 engine does not support lookahead.
Rewrite lookahead-based examples using supported matching patterns.
Review source

column1: Why is (\w+)\1 not a supported SQL Server regex matching pattern?
column2:
RE2 does not support backreferences inside matching patterns.
Capture references in REGEXP_REPLACE replacement text are a separate feature.
Review source

column1: Which SQL Server 2025 function replaces text selected by a regex pattern?
column2:
REGEXP_REPLACE().
The pattern identifies the substrings to replace.
Review source

column1: How many matching occurrences does REGEXP_REPLACE replace by default?
column2:
All matching occurrences.
Its default occurrence argument is 0.
Review source

column1: What does REGEXP_REPLACE return when no pattern match exists?
column2:
The original input string.
No matching substring is available to replace.
Review source

column1: What does an empty replacement string do in REGEXP_REPLACE?
column2:
Removes the matched substrings.
Use '' to remove matches instead of substituting visible text.
Review source

column1: Which SQL Server 2025 function extracts one matching substring?
column2:
REGEXP_SUBSTR().
Use it when the matched text is needed rather than only its position.
Review source

column1: What does REGEXP_SUBSTR return when no match exists?
column2:
NULL.
A missing match is not returned as an empty string.
Review source

column1: What does REGEXP_SUBSTR's occurrence argument select?
column2:
Which matching occurrence to return.
The default value 1 selects the first match.
Review source

column1: What does REGEXP_SUBSTR's group argument select?
column2:
Which capture group's text to return.
The default group 0 selects the complete match.
Review source

column1: Which SQL Server 2025 function returns a match's starting position by default?
column2:
REGEXP_INSTR().
It returns a position rather than the matched text.
Review source

column1: What position does REGEXP_INSTR use for a match at the first character?
column2:
1.
Character positions are 1-based.
Review source

column1: What does REGEXP_INSTR return when no match exists?
column2:
0.
This differs from REGEXP_SUBSTR's NULL result for a missing match.
Review source

column1: Which SQL Server 2025 function counts matches of a regex pattern?
column2:
REGEXP_COUNT().
Its result is an integer count.
Review source

column1: What does REGEXP_COUNT('A12 B345','\d+') return?
column2:
2.
Each consecutive digit run is one match.
Review source

column1: Which SQL Server 2025 function splits text into rows using a delimiter pattern?
column2:
REGEXP_SPLIT_TO_TABLE().
The pattern describes separators rather than the tokens to return.
Review source

column1: If a nonempty string has no delimiter match, what does REGEXP_SPLIT_TO_TABLE return?
column2:
One row containing the original string.
The input remains one unsplit token.
Review source

column1: What does REGEXP_SPLIT_TO_TABLE's ordinal column identify?
column2:
The token's 1-based position in the input.
Use ORDER BY ordinal when output order matters.
Review source

column1: Which APPLY operator expands each product's Tags into rows with REGEXP_SPLIT_TO_TABLE?
column2:
CROSS APPLY.
The function call can reference the current product's Tags column.
Review source

column1: Which SQL Server 2025 function returns all pattern matches as a rowset?
column2:
REGEXP_MATCHES().
Unlike splitting, the pattern describes the text to keep.
Review source

column1: What does REGEXP_MATCHES return when no match exists?
column2:
No rows.
It does not return a placeholder row containing NULL.
Review source

column1: Which REGEXP_MATCHES column contains the complete matched text?
column2:
match_value.
This is separate from the capture-group details.
Review source

column1: Which REGEXP_MATCHES column describes capture groups as JSON?
column2:
substring_matches.
The JSON document includes details about the captured substrings.
Review source
